perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He and Jonathan have been close friends since childhood; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his more educated perspective.
- Christian is a police officer, which shapes his investigative actions.
- He feels anxious and suspicious that Jonathan is hiding something important; he perceives Jonathan as acting differently.
- He arranged and attended a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. He heard Jonathan admit that he had been keeping something from him, that he was in trouble, and that he had not known how to tell him.
- Christian offered to help and support Jonathan. He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated, that he did not want to drag Christian into it, but that he could use support and resources and needed to get out of a mess.
- Christian asked whether Jonathan’s trouble was related to illegal activity. He heard Jonathan say he could not say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian decided to look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his investigation, Christian came to believe/learn that Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this, said he had leads but was not sure who was responsible yet, and decided to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later believed/claimed he had found out who was behind it: someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He decided to confront that person and bring them to justice.
- He heard Jonathan warn that this person is dangerous and express trust that Christian would do what is right.
- The specific identity of the culprit is not stated in the dialogue available to Christian.
